Usage: fshw [global options] <command>

FsHotWatch — F# file watcher daemon
Global options:
  --verbose, -v                Enable debug-level logging (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_VERBOSE)
  --log-level, -l <string>     Set log level: error|warning|info|debug (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_LOG_LEVEL)
  --no-cache                   Disable on-disk task result cache (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_NO_CACHE)
  --no-warn-fail               Treat warnings as non-fatal (errors still fail) (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_NO_WARN_FAIL)
  --compact, -q                Compact one-line-per-plugin output (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_COMPACT)
  --agent, -a                  Agent-friendly parseable output with next-step hint (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_AGENT)

Commands:
  start            Start the daemon
  stop             Stop the daemon
  check            Run all checks. The fast inner loop — the tests are IMPACT-FILTERED, which is a latency optimization and not the basis for a merge decision (use `confirm` for that)
  confirm          Run the FULL suite and confirm `check` told the truth.
                   Any disagreement is a BUG:
                     failed here, not selected by check  → the selector MISSED a test
                     passed here, but check says failed  → a stale red, a flake, or a
                                                           test that only passes with company
                   Refuses a green verdict from anything less than the full suite (exit 3).
  verdict          Report the last check's verdict and whether it still applies to the current tree (reads .fshw/verdict.json; never contacts the daemon)
  test-rerun       Rerun tests with an xUnit v3 --filter-class / --filter-trait slice
  format           Format code
  status [plugin]  Show current status
  scan             Scan for file changes
  invalidate       Invalidate cached task results without stopping the daemon
  rerun <plugin-name> Force a plugin to re-run, clearing its cached state
  init             Generate initial config
  config           Configuration commands
  coverage         Coverage

result.stdout:
Usage: fshw test-rerun [options]

Rerun tests with an xUnit v3 --filter-class / --filter-trait slice

Options:
  --filter-class <string>      Pass --filter-class <pattern> to the underlying test runner (xUnit v3) (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_FILTER_CLASS)
  --filter-trait <string>      Pass --filter-trait <name=value> to the underlying test runner (xUnit v3) (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_FILTER_TRAIT)
  --project, -p <string>       Limit the rerun to this test project (repeatable; matches the project name in your test config). Without it the filter is fanned out across EVERY configured test project, so a class living in one of them makes all the others report zero matches. (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_PROJECT)
  --wait-sec, -w <int>         Seconds to wait for an in-flight background test run to release the slot before reporting busy (default 600). Raise it above a long tests.beforeRun chain so an explicit rerun isn't defeated. (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_WAIT_SEC)

Examples:
  fshw test-rerun --filter-class *CryptoTests*
  fshw test-rerun --filter-trait Category=Browser

Usage: fshw dead-code [options]

Options:
  --entry, -e <string>         Entry-point name pattern (repeatable; replaces the defaults: *.main, *.Program.*, *.Routes.*, *.Scheduler.*) (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_ENTRY)
  --include-tests, -i          Include symbols from test files in the report (env: FS_HOT_WATCH_INCLUDE_TESTS)

Examples:
  fshw dead-code 
  fshw dead-code --include-tests
  fshw dead-code --entry *.Cli.* --entry *.Worker.*
